claim: The hook dispatch reads the page index to learn which hooks judge a call, and `hook-dispatch.module.code.ts:155-158` refuses before it reads the event or the tool name, so an index it cannot read refuses every tool call at every event. The CLI beneath that guard is built for a missing index: `calling.module.code.ts:111-117` routes `index refresh` without consulting the index, and `:203-206` tells the reader to say exactly that. The guard has no such arm. On 2026-09-13 `2e262f81512` repointed the index at `.index` and nothing had written it there; two hook cost ledgers hold the same hole, 14:40:21Z to 14:41:25Z, closing in the second `.index/value/agent-hook.jsonl` was filed. Nothing recorded the outage, because the refusing arm returns before a cost is written. A person ran the refresh from outside the harness.

evidence:
Read and measured 2026-09-13, hours after the window closed.

The move. `2e262f81512`, 08:40:21-0600, touches six files under `page/index/`. `index-surface.module.code.ts` drops `gitFolderIn`, its `sharedIn` memo and the `GIT_AT` and `INDEXES` imports, and gains `INDEX_AT` as `.index` at `:14`, so `indexIn(root)` at `:22-24` is now plain `join(root, INDEX_AT)`. Reader and writer take that one function — `index-reading.module.code.ts:72` reading, `index-filing.module.code.ts:36` and `:42` and `indexing.module.code.ts:199` and `:207` writing — so this was no split landing, and no stale process either, the dispatch spawning fresh per call. Both sides were repointed together at a store holding nothing. `.git/index` was left where it was, last written 2026-09-12 06:52; `.index` was born 08:41:06. The staging was careful: `0c2ba5aaedf` at 08:34:32 had already put `.index` into `.gitignore` and `.dockerignore`.

Where the guard reads. `hook-dispatch.module.code.ts:202` takes `rootOf(realpathSync(import.meta.path))` — not a constant and not a config, but the checkout holding the dispatch file, walked up to `akasha.domain.ts` by `rooting.module.code.ts:18-28`. All seven registration symlinks under `~/.local/state/akasha/hooks/` point at that one file, so every session on this machine resolved the same root whatever its cwd. `hooksIn` at `:94-102` calls `valuesOfType` inside a bare catch. `index-reading.module.code.ts:82-86` throws when the reading does not hold its root, wording it with the constant at `:61`: an index that is missing is not an index naming none. The bare catch discards exactly that distinction, so a missing index reaches `answerFor` as zero hooks and `:155-158` refuses with `decision: block` at code 2 by `hook-answer.module.code.ts:72-78`. Memoisation is per `Reading` object through the WeakMaps at `:90-119`, and `readingIn` makes a fresh one per string root, so nothing is held across calls. `:155-158` runs before `:160` reads the event and before `heldFor` filters by tool, so the refusal depends on neither. The sixteen `*.agent-hook.ts` pages were on disk throughout and are there still.

The window, observed. `weigh-bash-call.agent-hook.entries.uncommitted.jsonl` records one line per call the dispatch ran that hook for. Its lines sit one to three seconds apart on either side, and it holds nothing between 14:40:20Z and 14:41:26Z. `block-akasha-shell-writes.agent-hook.entries.uncommitted.jsonl` holds nothing between 14:40:20Z and 14:41:25Z. The commit is 14:40:21Z. `.index/value/agent-hook.jsonl` was written at 14:41:25.373Z, and that file is what the dispatch reads for its hooks, so the guard came back in the second the refresh filed it.

Why the repair was out of reach. `calling.module.code.ts:111-117` holds `ROOTED` as the two words `index refresh`, and `:409-412` routes exactly those two words to `indexRefresh` whenever `unreadIn` finds the index unread, ahead of any lookup. `:203-206` says so in the refusal it writes: every command is found through the index, so none is read without one, say `akasha index refresh`, which is answered without the index, and then say the call again. That repair path is deliberate, built, and works with no index at all. It is reached by running a command; running a command is a tool call; the tool call is what `:155-158` refused. The guard never looks at the input, so it has no arm that could let that one through. Alan ran the refresh from a shell outside the harness.

Nothing alarmed. `answerFor` returns at `:157` before `linksMade` at `:159` and before the loop calling `costKept` at `:176`, so a dispatch refusing everything writes no cost line at all. The outage is a hole in the ledger rather than an entry in it. `service-watching` reports on workstation systemd units and the dispatch is not one; `service-watching.module.ts:66-68` already carries a gap for its own silence. This was noticed because an agent's calls stopped while a person was sitting there.

Moving the index out of git's folder is approved work and is not the fault here. The gap is that no step writes the new store before the guard is repointed at it, and nothing can waive the guard for the one call that would write it.
